focus: Left post tib / arch + right shin · left Achilles is the main range limiter

phase.name: Calm it down
phase.exit: Walking and daily life pain-free 3+ straight days, and the daily dose itself fully green.

note: About 15 min daily. Before runs: doming, heel-raise hold, inversion hold. The rest any time that day. This is the LAST thing that gets dropped on a busy week.
pain_rules: Green: ≤3/10 working discomfort that settles within an hour, continue. Yellow: 4–5/10, or worse the next morning, back off a level. Red: sharp pain, limping, or pain at rest, stop that exercise. Get it looked at if the left arch looks flatter than the right, it swells behind the inside ankle bone, or you lose the single-leg heel raise.
special: HOLD (10/1): left Achilles 'giving way' episodes. No running, no left heel-raise holds or any left calf loading, no barefoot walking, until a doctor has examined the tendon (ultrasound). Doming, inversion holds, tib raises, side plank, and seated work are fine if pain-free.

exercises.name: Short-foot arch doming
exercises.cue: Squeeze and hold — pull the big-toe knuckle toward the heel, no toe curling. End the rep when the dome starts collapsing.

exercises.name: Isometric heel-raise hold
exercises.cue: Rise to half height and actively press the balls of the feet down for the whole hold, weight through the big toe. Shoes are fine. Skip the left if it isn't comfortable.

exercises.name: Isometric inversion hold
exercises.cue: Seated, foot flat. Push the inside edge of the foot inward against your other foot or a wall. Moderate effort, pain-free. The post tib's own hold; best right before a run.

exercises.name: Banded ankle inversion
exercises.cue: Band around the forefoot, sweep the foot inward — slow and controlled; this is the post tib's own exercise. No band? Ankle over the opposite knee, press the inside of the forefoot into your palm.

exercises.name: Tibialis raises (wall lean)
exercises.cue: Heels on the ground, lift both forefeet — front-side work for the right shin.

exercises.name: Side plank + top-leg raise
exercises.cue: Hips stacked, lift the top leg while holding the plank — the standing progression of your clamshells.

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.cue: Barefoot, soft knee — post tib + hip coordination, not filler. Progress: eyes closed.

exercises.name: Right-leg range work
exercises.cue: Right ankle range tested normal (11 cm knee-to-wall), so this is upkeep: calf stretch straight-knee and bent-knee, 45s each, plus a few knee-to-wall rocks. Massage gun on the right calf and inner shin for the tissue tightness the therapist felt. The left still gets no calf stretching.

also: Book a sports-medicine or orthopedic visit this week and ask for an Achilles ultrasound. Same day urgent care if: a pop, a dent in the tendon, the foot doesn't move when the calf is squeezed, or you can't rise on the left toes
Massage gun on calves, soleus, inner shin, and lower inner thigh, 1–5 min per area (muscle, not tendon or bone)
Supportive non-plated trainers all day; no flip-flops or barefoot on hard floors
Desk and commute: every 30–45 min do 10 ankle pumps and a few doming holds, or stand and walk a minute; keep shoes on
Evening: hot tub then cold plunge (finish cold), and/or Normatec
Gym days: adductor machine or short-lever Copenhagen, plus hip abduction
Mornings after runs: note post-tib stiffness at first steps and gently squeeze the low left Achilles

Sundays: single-leg heel raise both sides (film from behind to see if the heels turn in) + knee-to-wall in cm (right fully, left only to the first Achilles pull). Baseline 9/28: knee-to-wall L 9.5 (Achilles-limited), R 11; heel raise: both rise, neither heel visibly turns in, left harder to rise and balance
Next deep massage: Mon 10/5 or Tue 10/6
avoid: Sharp turns and pickleball for now (left turns flare the post tib)
Any left calf stretching; loaded end-range left calf work
The plated Hyperion; flat shoes, flip-flops, barefoot on hard floors
